cluster.headline: 1.6 מיליון חשבונות, 4.3 מיליארד שקל — כך הבנקים חוגגים על העמלות שלכם
cluster.body_note: Paywalled past lead paragraph (TheMarker .premium gate); no JSON-LD articleBody. Visible claims via WebFetch: ~1.6M independent trading accounts in Israel; NIS 4.3B in fee revenue from this segment in 2025; ~74% of that (~NIS 3.2B) stays with the banks; investment houses said to attract about half of new customers. Byline: Nati Tucker, published 25.10.2026 06:10. No regulator (Bank of Israel / Securities Authority / Capital Markets Authority) named as source in the visible text.

primary_source_search.source_name: No primary source located for the NIS 4.3B / 74% figures. Partial/contextual sources: Meitav investment-house estimate of >1.6M securities trading accounts (via Globes, 17.07.2026); TASE new-account data (via Calcalist); Bank of Israel Banking Supervision household fee report for 2025 and H1 2025; BoI/ISA/Treasury joint team final report 'Compensation Models in the Public's Securities Activity' (24.06.2026, press release only reachable, full Hebrew report not located; ynet coverage cites NIS 3.5B for the five big banks).

verified_figures.trading_accounts_total: >1.6M securities trading accounts in Israel — Meitav investment house estimate (Globes 17.07.2026); total accounts, not specifically 'independent'/self-directed
verified_figures.bank_accounts_split_2023: ~900K portfolios at banks (~650K self-directed, ~350K advised) vs ~150K at non-bank brokers, end-2023 (ynet, citing BoI data)
verified_figures.new_accounts_share: Non-bank TASE members' share of new accounts ~7% (2019) -> ~47% (2024) per joint-team report coverage (ynet); 53% of 2024 new accounts at banks (Globes); ~53K of ~101K new accounts through Oct 2025 (~52%) at investment houses per TASE data (Calcalist)
verified_figures.bank_trading_fees_2025: NIS 3.5B record trading-fee revenue for the five largest banks in 2025, +18.4% y/y (ynet coverage of joint-team final report; full report not reached)
verified_figures.boi_household_fees_2025: Bank fee income from households + small businesses NIS 5.7B in 2025 vs 5.4B in 2024, rise mainly due to securities activity (BoI press release); securities ~29% of H1 2025 household/small-biz fee income (BoI H1 2025 report)
verified_figures.portfolio_share: ~85% of investment portfolios still held at banks (ynet, joint-team coverage)
